standard.title: Modelling with Ratios and Rates
standard.description: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving ratios and rates, including financial contexts; formulate problems; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, reviewing the appropriateness of the model
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can solve ratio and rate problems (from AC9M7M06, AC9M8M05). Students have modelling experience from prior years.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students formulate and solve models for practical problems involving ratios and rates in financial and scientific contexts, review appropriateness and communicate solutions.

nodes.label: Formulating and solving ratio/rate models
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students identify whether a problem requires a ratio or rate model, formulate it, and solve in context.
nodes.minimum_width: Formulate and solve a practical problem using either a ratio or rate model; state which is appropriate and why.
nodes.typical_width: Apply modelling to scales and plans, chemical mixing, currency conversion, and income tax; justify model choice; select efficient calculation strategy.
wider: Investigate radiocarbon dating as a ratio application: model the ratio of carbon-14 to carbon-12 isotopes in organic material to estimate age.
Model the ratio applications in First Nations Australians' string and cordage making — investigate the ratio of fibre lengths and twisting rates involved.

response_modes.reason: Ratio and rate modelling problems span an unusually wide range of contexts at Year 8. Multiple varied contexts are needed to build the judgment to select the right model structure.

nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires evaluating model appropriateness — students who have only formulated one model type cannot identify when the chosen model oversimplifies or when a different structure would be more appropriate.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Radiocarbon dating as a ratio context offers advancing students a genuinely rich scientific application — connecting the abstract ratio concept to a real archaeological and environmental science method is compelling and within Year 8 reach.
success_criteria: Correctly identifies whether the problem requires a ratio or rate model.
Formulates and solves the model correctly.
Justifies the model choice and interprets the solution in context.

nodes.label: Reviewing model appropriateness
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students evaluate whether a ratio or rate model is appropriate for a given situation, identify assumptions, and suggest improvements.
nodes.minimum_width: State one assumption in a given model and explain how it might limit the model's accuracy.
nodes.typical_width: Review the appropriateness of a model for varied practical contexts; identify when a simple ratio/rate model oversimplifies; suggest model refinements.
wider: Compare simple and refined models for the same situation (e.g. constant vs variable exchange rate) — evaluate which is more appropriate and in what circumstances.
Investigate a financial model (income tax brackets) and evaluate where the 'step function' model differs from a smooth rate model — discuss the implications.

response_modes.reason: Reviewing model appropriateness requires coordinating modelling experience, real-world knowledge, and mathematical reasoning simultaneously — the integration of the whole measurement modelling strand.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one assumption made in a given model.
Explains how the assumption affects the model's accuracy.
Suggests a reasonable refinement to the model.
